{{Short description|Vector bundle associated with conformal manifolds}}
In [[differential geometry]], the '''local twistor bundle''' is a specific [[vector bundle]] with [[connection (vector bundle)|connection]] that can be associated to any [[conformal manifold]], at least locally.  Intuitively, a local twistor is an association of a [[twistor space]] to each point of space-time, together with a conformally invariant connection that relates the twistor spaces at different points.  This connection can have [[holonomy]] that obstructs the existence of "global" twistors (that is, solutions of the twistor equation in open sets).

==Construction==
Let ''M'' be a pseudo-Riemannian conformal manifold with a [[spin structure]] and a conformal metric of signature (''p'',''q'').  The conformal group is the [[pseudo-orthogonal group]] <math>SO(p+1,q+1)</math>.  There is a [[Cartan connection|conformal Cartan connection]] on a bundle, the [[tractor bundle]], of ''M''.  The [[spin group]] of <math>SO(p+1,q+1)</math> admits a fundamental representation, the [[spin representation]], and the [[associated bundle]] is the local twistor bundle.

==Representation via Weyl spinors==
Local twistors can be represented as pairs of [[Weyl spinor]]s on ''M'' (in general from different spin representations, determined by the reality conditions specific to the signature).  In the case of a four-dimensional [[Lorentzian manifold]], such as the space-time of general relativity, a local twistor has the form
:<math>Z^\alpha = \begin{bmatrix}\omega^A\\\pi_{A'}\end{bmatrix}.</math>
Here we use index conventions from {{harvtxt|Penrose|Rindler|1986}}, and <math>\omega^A</math> and <math>\pi_{A'}</math> are two-component complex spinors for the Lorentz group <math>SL(2,\mathbb C)</math>.

==Local twistor transport==
The connection, sometimes called ''local twistor transport'', is given by
:<math>dZ^\alpha = \begin{bmatrix}d\omega^A - i\theta^{AA'}\pi_{A'}\\ d\pi_{A'}-iP_{AA'}\omega^A\end{bmatrix}.</math>
Here <math>\theta^{AA'}</math> is the [[canonical one-form]] and <math>P_{AA'}</math> the [[Schouten tensor]], contracted on one index with the canonical one-form.  An analogous equation holds in other dimensions, with appropriate [[Clifford algebra]] multipliers between the two Weyl spin representations {{harv|Sparling|1986}}.  In this formalism, the [[twistor equation]] is the requirement that a local twistor be parallel under the connection.

==Canonical filtration==
In general, the local twistor bundle ''T'' is equipped with a [[short exact sequence]] of vector bundles
:<math>0\to \Pi\to T\to \Omega\to 0</math>
where <math>\Pi</math> and <math>\Omega</math> are two Weyl spin bundles.  The bundle <math>\Pi</math> is a distinguished sub-bundle, that corresponds to the marked point of contact of the conformal Cartan connection.  That is, there is a canonical marked one-dimensional subspace ''X'' in the tractor bundle, and <math>\Pi</math> is the annihilator of ''X'' under Clifford multipliction.  In four dimensions, <math>\Pi</math> is the space of spinors <math>\pi_{A'}</math> and <math>\Omega</math> the space of <math>\omega^A</math>.  Under the [[Plücker embedding]], the tractor bundle in four dimensions is isomorphic to the [[exterior algebra|exterior square]] of the local twistor bundle, and <math>\Pi</math> consists of all the twistors incident with
:<math>X^{\alpha\beta}=\begin{bmatrix}0&0\\ 0&\epsilon_{A'B'}\end{bmatrix}</math>
where <math>\epsilon_{A'B'}</math> is the symplectic form on <math>\Pi</math>.

==Curvature==
The curvature of the local twistor connection involves both the [[Weyl curvature]] and the [[Cotton tensor]].  (It is the Cartan conformal curvature.)  The curvature preserves the space <math>\Pi</math>, and on <math>\Pi</math> it involves only the conformally-invariant Weyl curvature.
